terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.intro: Welcome to MARES. By requesting access or activating your account, you agree to the terms below, which govern the use of this platform for recording and analyzing pathological data of marine fauna occurrences.
terms.acceptLabel: I have read and accept the <link>Terms of Use</link>

data.title: 1. Data and purpose
data.body: The data recorded is intended for scientific research on marine fauna. Each research group is responsible for the data it enters and for ensuring authorization to collect and process it.

usage.title: 2. Platform use
usage.body: Access is personal and non-transferable. You agree to keep your credentials confidential and to use the platform only for legitimate research and conservation purposes.

privacy.title: 3. Privacy
privacy.body: We collect only the data required to operate the service (name, email and research group memberships). We do not share your personal data with third parties without a legal basis.

responsibility.title: 4. Responsibilities
responsibility.body: The accuracy of scientific data is the responsibility of whoever records it. The platform is provided as is, without guarantees of uninterrupted availability.

deletion.title: 5. Profile deletion and data permanence
deletion.body: You can delete your profile at any time from the "My profile" area. Deletion removes your account data (name, email and memberships) and ends your access, but does NOT delete scientific data already published on the platform (animals, samples, analyses and research): it remains recorded to preserve scientific integrity and is no longer associated with you. If a research group is left with no members, it is deactivated, and its public data stays visible on the public map.

changes.title: 6. Changes
changes.body: These terms may be updated. When that happens, you may be asked to accept them again on your next sign-in. The date of the current version is shown at the top of this page.

tutorial.title: How to use MARES
tutorial.subtitle: The platform's standard flow, from access to export. Open each topic to see the steps.

overview.title: Overview and roles
overview.body: MARES organizes the recording of marine fauna occurrences by research group. Below is the standard usage flow.
points: Application admin: approves requests and oversees groups and users; does not access scientific data.
Research group admin: manages members, research, protocols and the glossary.
Researcher: creates and edits animals, samples and analyses — only in the research they are assigned to.
Public: without login, sees only data marked as public.

access.title: 1. Platform access
access.body: To get started, you need an account linked to a research group.
points: Request access on the public screen (creates a new group) or ask a group admin to invite you by email.
You receive an email with a link to set your password. The link expires on first use; if needed, the admin resends the invite.
After signing in, adjust your name and password in 'My profile'.

group.title: 2. Research group and members
group.body: The research group is your team's environment. Member management is done by the group admin.
points: In 'Members', the admin adds researchers by email (the lookup reuses existing accounts).
Roles: group admin (manages everything) or researcher. The last admin cannot step down.
Researchers access 'Members' and 'Glossary' in read-only mode.

glossary.title: 3. Glossary (biological materials, pathogens, exams, systems)
glossary.body: The glossary holds the standardized terms used in protocols and analyses.
points: Biological materials, pathogens, exam types and anatomical systems are global and shared across groups.
Any group admin can add terms; editing/removing is restricted to the application admin.
Pathogens use the scientific name; exams may have a quantitative measure (e.g. Ct).
Anatomical systems start empty: register the ones your group's protocol uses, and they become available to necropsy reports.
Cannot edit an item (you did not register it, or it is already in use)? Use 'Suggest an edit' — a curator applies the change.

research.title: 4. Research and protocol
research.body: Each study is a 'research', which defines the protocol and who can see its data.
points: Create the research under 'Researches' and set up the protocol: material × pathogen × exam combinations.
Everyone in the group CAN SEE the research list (name, description, owner), but the data — animals, samples and analyses — belongs only to its members.
Not a member and need the data? Use 'Request access' in the list; whoever created the research (or the group admin) approves.
Requests awaiting your answer appear at the top of the 'Researches' screen. Approving links the person to the research.
Set the research visibility (public or private).

animal.title: 5. Register the animal (individual)
animal.body: The animal represents the physical individual in the occurrence.
points: Register under 'Animals', choosing the originating research. You can import SIMBA data by record number.
Before filling in the rest, use the magnifier next to the control ID to check whether the individual already exists in the group — including in researches you cannot access.
Occurrence fields (date, place, coordinates) can be marked as 'no information' when unavailable.
The animal's effective public visibility requires both it AND the research to be public.
The control ID and SIMBA number are unique across the whole group: if another research already registered the individual, the record is rejected — see the next topic.

sharing.title: 6. Sharing individuals between researches
sharing.body: The same individual can be studied by more than one research in the group, with no duplicate record. The link only counts when both researches agree.
points: On the animal page, under 'Researches', pick another research in the group to share the individual with.
If that research is not yours, an invitation is sent: it must accept before seeing the individual (until then it shows as 'pending').

The other way around: when you register an animal whose control ID or SIMBA number already exists in a research you cannot access, the warning offers to request the individual — the originating research decides.
Requests and invitations awaiting YOUR answer appear at the top of the 'Animals' screen.
Sharing grants access to the individual (identity, occurrence), never to the other research's samples and analyses — each keeps its own.

necropsy.title: 7. Necropsy (pathology report)
necropsy.body: The animal's 'Necropsy' tab holds both halves of the report: the gross exam, by anatomical system, and the histopathology exam, by organ. The report belongs to the INDIVIDUAL — on a shared individual, both researches see and edit the same report.
points: Start by adding to the report the systems this necropsy covered. The list comes from the glossary; if a system is missing, register it there first.
Each system gets a state: 'altered' (which opens the findings table), 'no change', or 'not examined', which requires the reason (e.g. autolysis).
A system in the report without a state shows as 'not assessed' — different from 'no change', which asserts it was examined and nothing was found.
Each gross finding has topography (organ, tissue and site), lesion, distribution, severity and the parasite fields.
For parasites, 'not informed' is not the same as 'no': mark 'no' only when you looked and found none. Count is only editable if the parasites were collected.
In the histopathology exam, record one organ → finding pair at a time. The dialog stays open for entering several in a row.
Marking a system as 'no change' or 'not examined' is refused while it still has findings — remove them first; nothing is deleted automatically.

samples.title: 8. Samples
samples.body: Samples are collected per biological material of the individual, in the animal's 'Samples' tab.
points: Register each sample with biological material, type, status and storage location.
The material selector lists only the protocol's materials; use 'Show all' for opportunistic/biobank collection.

analyses.title: 9. Analyses and results
analyses.body: Analyses record the lab results per sample.
points: The grid combines the protocol's material × pathogen × exam; mark each result (positive, negative or inconclusive) and the measure, when applicable.
Positive results appear as 'positive pathogens' in the listing and filters.

history.title: 10. Animal history
history.body: Each individual has a timeline of changes.
points: The 'History' tab gathers animal edits, sample creation/edits and analysis changes, with author and date.

map.title: 11. Map and public data
map.body: Occurrences appear on a browsable map.
points: The internal map shows the animals you can see; the public map (no login) shows only the effectively public ones.
Filter the animals list by species, state, pathogen, research, period and more.

export.title: 12. Export
export.body: Export the data for external analysis.
points: Select animals (or use 'select all' from the current filter) and export as Excel or Darwin Core.
The spreadsheet has three sheets: Animals (one row per individual), Pathology report (gross and histopathology findings, with an 'Exam' column telling them apart) and Analyses.
The Animals sheet includes a 'Descriptive diagnosis' column, built from the histopathology findings in SIMBA's running-text format.
